column1: # The trust lane's cost-history SEED: the fallback a clone with no history of its own reads (a library's newer row of this file and its git directory's aterm-release/trust-costs.tsv is the one read). `targo --unverified ship trust run -p <crate>… --update-ratchet` rewrites it with floors.tsv and memory.tsv. A library in neither file runs first, claiming 16 GiB or half the RAM, whichever is less.

# trust lane cost history: <name> <CPU s> <wall s> <largest process's peak RSS bytes> <when>; the slots take the longest first, a library with no row first of all, and each check claims its peak and a margin before it starts (a claim not below what can ever be available, the RAM less what is wired, is refused up front)
